name: Abruzzi
description: In October 2018 we acquired a seven-story terraced building with mixed-use units in Vialle Abruzzi, Milan, situated close to the central station.
Following the purchase, our strategy was to refurbish the common areas and façades in addition to elevating the roof and creating 15 residential units.

name: Apollo Portfolio
description: In June 2016 iAM Capital acquired and consolidated a portfolio of 31 solar energy fields located in southern and northern Italy with an installed capacity of 34.5 MWp.

name: Bressanone
description: The asset located at Via Bressanone comprises of 2,364 gross sqm (1,994 net sqm) of office space over 4 floors in a semi-central area of Milan to the Northwest of the city.
The building was vacant at purchase and offered the opportunity both for conversion into modern loft-style office space or residential use.

name: CAR Portfolio
description: In June 2021 iAM Capital acquired a 4.5 MWp solar PV portfolio in Southern Italy comprised of 5 PV fields. The plan was to improve the efficiency of the assets on the technical side through soft works and production maximization.

name: Capo Mimosa
description: In March 2023, we acquired Capo Mimosa, a beachfront property in Cervo, Liguria to develop a contemporary, five-star beach resort with 90 suites, as well as a beach club, a restaurant and state of the art spa facilities.'
The asset is situated on 5.5 hectares of prime seafront land on a hill with unobstructed, panoramic views of the Mediterranean sea.

name: Castel Porrona
description: In March 2026, we acquired Castel Porrona, a historic hospitality asset located in the Tuscan countryside near Montalcino, through our ICE III Fund. The property is a fortified borgo dating back to the 15th century, comprising a central tower and a collection of traditional stone buildings enclosed within the original medieval village walls.
The asset includes approximately 30 rooms and suites, together with a restaurant, spa and wellness facilities, and an outdoor swimming pool.

name: Cañizares
description: In December 2025, iAM Capital acquired a centrally located hostel asset at Cañizares in Madrid. CATS Hostels will operate the property going forward. The asset benefits from walking-distance access to major landmarks and strong year-round demand from international travellers. The business plan focuses on operational optimisation and guest-experience upgrades.

name: Depretis
description: The asset located at Via Depretis comprised of a trophy building containing c. 7,000 sqm of prime office space in Rome.

In parallel to the negotiations with the vendor and the incumbent lender, we identified two strategies; conversion into high quality residential units, or hotel use. Following the negotiations with a German hotel operator that was looking for a prime location in Rome, the asset was sold 3 months after closing at a significant premium to the acquisition price.

name: Fulvio Testi
description: The asset located at Viale Fulvio Testi consisted of 2,626 gross sqm (1,972 net sqm) of office space located on the outskirts of Bicocca, a semi-central neighborhood of Milan.

The strategy was to convert the asset into residential.
We exited our investment in May of 2022.

name: Galerie St. Marc
description: In August 2019, we acquired a property in Galerie Saint Marc, Paris, comprised of the Basement, Ground, First, and Second floors of the building.
Following the capex works our strategy was to refurbish into 5 short-term units and lease to an operating partner.

name: Gobetti
description: The asset at Via Gobetti is a 10,497 gross sqm office building in an office park located 15km from the city of Milan in Cernusco sul Naviglio.
Our strategy was to lightly renew the interior in order to re-lease the space and exit upon stabilisation.

name: Govone
description: The asset, acquired in July 2021, consists of 2,203 gross sqm (1,844 net sqm) over five floors spread across two buildings in Northern Milan. One building comprised of three retail spaces on the ground floor and 14 residential units above. The second building included 400 sqm of office and laboratory space.
We exited our investment in December of 2022.

name: Murat
description: In early December 2021, we acquired the building at Via Gioacchino Murat. Located in northern Milan, the office asset was a 2,549 gross sqm building over three floors and six parking spaces.
The building was identified as a strong candidate for conversion into residences since the building was well suited for fractioning into separate units.
The conversion works have now been completed, successfully transforming the asset into high-quality residential units in line with our initial repositioning strategy.

name: Palazzo Sanzio
description: In August 2022, we acquired a trophy asset in Rome, a c. 6,000 sqm building over five floors located at Lungotevere Raffaello Sanzio.

Situated opposite the Isola Tiberina, one of the most popular neighborhoods of the Italian capital, the investment strategy entails conversion into 5-star luxury hotel with a rooftop restaurant, where 360 views of the city center and the Vatican are available.
Reservations though Palazzo Sanzio Radisson Collection.

name: Pasealekua
description: In December 2025, iAM Capital acquired a hostel asset in San Sebastián, located approximately five minutes from Playa de Ondarreta. CATS Hostels will operate the property going forward. The asset benefits from strong tourism demand and a prime coastal micro-location within walking distance of the city’s most popular beaches. The business plan targets operational efficiencies and guest-experience upgrades.

name: Patay
description: In October 2021, we finalized the acquisition of one of our earliest pipeline assets for ICE II, located in southeast Paris, at Rue de Patay. The asset consists of 1,960 gross sqm of mixed-use office and retail space that was underlet at purchase.
The investment strategy is to vacate and re-let the asset at market rent.

name: Quai Bourbon
description: In early July 2021, we completed the acquisition of two super-prime trophy assets. The combined asset consists of 185 gross sqm across 3 floors.

The second-floor unit has been refurbished to a very high standard, which is now going to be rented out to a leading short-term letting business. The remaining two units will follow the same strategy.

name: Ravignan & Berthe
description: In early 2017, we acquired two apartment units in Rue de Ravignan and Rue Berthe, central Paris, both located in the Montmartre district.
Following the acquisition, the strategy is to repurpose these two residential units and re-let them at market rates to a leading short-term letting business.

name: Repubblica
description: Just before the end of 2021, we acquired a small 2-unit residential asset located at Piazza Repubblica, one of Milan’s most exclusive residential areas, within walking distance from the central station. The asset consists of c. 300 sqm on the second floor of a well-maintained building, a balcony, a parking space, and two cellars and a loft.
Our strategy for the asset is to break-up the 2 apartments into 3 residential units to be fitted out and leased to a short-term rental operator, given the excellent location.

name: Roquette
description: In November 2015 we completed the acquisition of a building comprised of 3 shops and approximately 20 residential units.
Our strategy is to extensively renovate the property, and then break/up and sell the units independently at a premium.

name: Saint Ouen
description: At the end of 2018, we completed the acquisition of a property located at 11 Avenue de Saint Ouen in Paris.

With a total of 790sqm, their previous rents were quite below market and following the purchase, our objective was to carry out extensive renovation works and to resell the units independently within 2 years of purchase.

name: Santa Marta
description: In December 2025, iAM Capital acquired a hostel asset in Córdoba’s historic centre. CATS Hostels will operate the property going forward. The asset features a traditional Cordoban patio with an outdoor swimming pool and benefits from a prime location within walking distance of key cultural landmarks. The strategy focuses on operational improvements and repositioning.

name: Sevres
description: In early 2017, we acquired one apartment unit in Rue de Sevres, central Paris, located in the Saint-Germain-des-Prés district.
Following the acquisition, the strategy is to renovate the apartment and re-let this out at market rates to a leading short-term letting business.

name: Sirtori
description: In mid-July 2021, we acquired the asset at Via Sirtori, which consisted of eight unfinished residential units and a loft area with extra high ceilings across c. 850 sqm.

Following the CapEx works, we created six residential units and a state of the art office unit. We have since leased the residential units to Sweetstay, a leading short-term rental operator, to capitalize on the post-pandemic travel boom and put the office space up for sale.

name: Temple
description: In early 2017, we acquired 4 ground floor apartments in Rue de Temple, central Paris, in the sought-after Marais district. Following the acquisition, the strategy was to renovate the units and re-let this out at market rates to a leading short-term letting business.

name: Torino
description: In May 2017, we acquired a mixed-use seven-story building, located in one of Milan’s shopping districts, that comprises eight office units and three retail spaces.
The strategy is to refurbish and re-let the retail space to comprise three state-of-the-art shops and sell the office units as-is.

name: UMJA Portfolio
description: Project UMJA is part of the iAM Capital buy and build strategy in the solar market through the consolidation of 4 plants singularly acquired and then combined into a larger 3.5 MWp portfolio. The portfolio’s larger size will make the transaction appealing to players with larger investment tickets.

name: Valassina
description: In early 2020, we acquired a five-story building, in Via Valassina, Milan. The building comprises 1,503 sqm with retail units at ground level and 4 floors with 12 residential units.
The strategy consists of restructuring the common parts and recovering the attic floor.
We exited our investment in May of 2022.
